[ASSISTANT_SAID] Homemade jam can last for 6 to 12 months in the fridge, best consumed within 6 months for optimal flavor and texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To store homemade jam, use a clean, sterilized glass jar with a tight-fitting lid and keep it in the refrigerator below 40°F (4°C).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Frozen jam can last for up to 12 months at 0°F (-18°C) or below.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Canned jam can last for 12 to 18 months at room temperature if processed in a water bath canner.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggestions for desserts using homemade jam include jam-filled cookies, jam-topped yogurt or ice cream, cakes and muffins, tarts and galettes, jam-filled crepes, fruit salad, cheesecake, jam-filled eclairs, custard-filled pastries, and fruit smoothie bowls.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Using bread flour in cookies can create a chewier and denser texture.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for using bread flour include adjusting liquid content, avoiding overmixing, allowing dough to rest, and monitoring baking time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For making croissants, use a reliable recipe, high-quality ingredients, respect the dough, laminate correctly, and keep the dough cool.
